blockers_on_product.title: Handling POC delivery settings
blockers_on_product.issue: Do we need to add support for all the channels since currently only hardcoded EMAIL template is supported
context: POC notifications on master: the complete flow
There are two notifications. Both send an HTML email to brand POCs through the OLD comm path (comm-sdk CommSvcClient → NSAdmin). PM/veyron isn't involved, and there's no "send test" feature.
│                           │          A. Offer-expiry reminder           │                  B. Issual-limit alert                  │
│ Configured in             │ Settings page (org level)                   │ Settings (recipients) + series form (threshold)         │
│ Triggered by              │ Daily cron at 10:00                         │ A coupon issuance that crosses the threshold            │
│ Delivered to Dracarys via │ RMQ scheduler-internal / dracarys_scheduler │ RMQ dracarys_exchange / coupon_limit_notification_queue │
1. Setup
Org settings (A + B recipients)
1. UI: Settings loads the POC list from IRIS GET /iris/v2/org/campaign/meta/pocs. You pick emails, but the UI sends userIds.
- Payload fields: voucherExpiryReminderEnabled, reminderDaysBeforeExpiry, reminderHourOfDay (fixed at 10), reminderUserIds, couponLimitNotifyUserIds.
- Sent as POST /coupon/api/v1/orgSettings.
2. Node: parseOrgSettingRequest JSON-encodes the id lists, then calls thrift saveOrgDefaults on Luci.
3. Luci:
- Rewrites the whole luci.default_properties set for the org: marks every row invalid, then inserts the new ones.
- If the reminder is enabled, registers the daily cron task (ORG_VOUCHER_EXPIRY_REMINDER) with the Cron service and records it in luci.task_scheduler_meta.
- If it's disabled, closes the task.
Series threshold (B)
1. UI: The series form sends "Notify when N coupons remaining" as POST /coupon/api/v1/config.
2. Node: Sends notifyCouponDeficiencyLimit = N (or -1) in thrift saveCouponConfiguration.
3. Luci:
- Rejects the save if N ≥ 0 and no POC ids are set.
- Stores NOTIFY_COUPON_LIMIT_DELTA in luci.coupon_config_key_values.
- Resets the Redis "already sent" flag.
2. Trigger

- A: Every day at 10:00, the Cron service publishes an RMQ message: headers org_id, reference_id=-1, event_type=EXECUTE, params={"jobType":"ORG_VOUCHER_EXPIRY_REMINDER"}. Dracarys sendCouponExpiryReminder then:
a. checks that the reminder is enabled;
b. selects series expiring exactly today + N days;
c. reads the POC ids.
- B: After every issuance, Luci checks whether max_create − issued ≤ N and the Redis flag isn't set. If so, it runs asynchronously:
a. takes a Redis lock;
b. publishes an RMQ message with an empty body and headers org_id, coupon_series_id;
c. sets the Redis flag (so it sends only once).
Dracarys sendCouponLimitNotification then reads the POC ids and loads that series.
3. Build and send (Dracarys, same for A and B)
1. Template: read from luci.org_voucher_expiry_reminder_message. If the org has none, the default is org 0, id -1 (A) or id -2 (B), seeded in cc-stack-crm.
2. Recipients: Arya GET /arya/api/v1/org/{org}/pocDetails, filtered to the configured userIds with a validated email.
3. Sender: user_management.custom_sender, formatted as label<replyto_email>.
4. Tags: filled once per series × POC:
- offer_name
- offer_expiry_date (yyyy-MM-dd)
- discount_details
- valid_on_products
- first_name
- remaining_coupons (B only)
- coupons_ui_url
5. Message: each one is an NSAdmin Message: EMAIL, priority HIGH, tag highvoltrans, clientId 3000, sent immediately. If any tag is left unfilled, that message is dropped.
6. Send: CommSvcClient.sendMultipleMessages, then NSAdmin delivers to the POC's inbox.
7. Log: one row per message in luci.voucher_reminder_messages_sent_yyyy_MM.
What the POC reads:
- A: "Offer expiry reminder - {offer}" … "Offer X is going to expire on {date}. Discount … valid on {products}." + a View / Edit offer link.
- B: "Offer coupon limit reminder - {offer}" … "Offer X has only {N} coupons remaining and is going to expire on {date} …" + the same link.
4. Data touched
│                            Store                            │                   Written by                   │    Read by     │
│ luci.default_properties (enable flag, days, hour, POC ids)  │ Luci                                           │ Luci, Dracarys │
│ luci.coupon_config_keys (defaults)                          │ seed                                           │ Luci, Dracarys │
│ luci.task_scheduler_meta                                    │ Luci                                           │ Luci           │
│ luci.coupon_config_key_values (NOTIFY_COUPON_LIMIT_DELTA)   │ Luci                                           │ Luci, Dracarys │
│ luci.voucher_series, owner_info, coupon_product_data_values │ Luci                                           │ Dracarys       │
│ luci.org_voucher_expiry_reminder_message (templates)        │ Dracarys thrift (nothing calls it in practice) │ Dracarys       │
│ luci.voucher_reminder_messages_sent_yyyy_MM                 │ Dracarys                                       │ nobody         │
│ user_management.custom_sender                               │ platform                                       │ Dracarys       │
│ Redis flag and lock (B)                                     │ Luci                                           │ Luci           │
Dracarys has no database of its own; it uses Luci's and Intouch's MySQL. Node stores nothing.
5. Known issues
- remaining_coupons shows the threshold N, not the live remaining count.
- valid_on_products is inverted. An offer restricted to specific products says "all products", and an unrestricted one says "selected products".
- The link is generic. It goes to the coupons home page ($INTOUCH_UI_BASE_URL/coupons/ui/), not the specific offer.
- POCs are listed and resolved by different services. The UI lists them from IRIS, but Dracarys resolves them through Arya. A user one returns and the other doesn't is silently skipped.
- Coupon uploads don't reset the limit flag, so once B has fired it won't fire again after more coupons are uploaded.
- Duplicate emails:
- A POC gets one email per expiring series.
- A has no guard against sending twice beyond the daily cron timing.
To test by hand: publish the RMQ message from step 2 for your org or series. That runs the real send.
